{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
{{Use New Zealand English|date=February 2024}}
Many of the national sports teams of [[New Zealand]] have been given nicknames, officially or otherwise, based on the iconic status of the [[All Blacks]] [[Rugby Union|rugby]] team, and (mostly in the case of female teams) the silver tree fern (''[[Cyathea dealbata]]'') of their logo.<ref name="TeAra-Wilson">{{Cite encyclopedia |title=Government and nation – Wearing the silver fern |encyclopedia=Te Ara – the Encyclopedia of New Zealand |url=http://www.teara.govt.nz/NewZealandInBrief/GovernmentAndNation/9/ENZ-Resources/Standard/7/en |access-date=17 September 2008 |date=23 September 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081019063803/http://www.teara.govt.nz/NewZealandInBrief/GovernmentAndNation/9/ENZ-Resources/Standard/7/en |archive-date=19 October 2008 |author=Wilson, John}}</ref> The practice became controversial when [[Badminton New Zealand]] used the name "Black Cocks" for a period in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 September 2005 |title=NZ finds Black Cocks hard to swallow |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2005/09/15/nz_badminton_kerfuffle/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060615182323/https://www.theregister.co.uk/2005/09/15/nz_badminton_kerfuffle/ |archive-date=15 June 2006 |access-date=5 September 2014 |website=[[The Register]]}}</ref>

|'''All Blacks'''
|[[New Zealand national rugby union team|Rugby union (men)]]
|During the ''[[The Original All Blacks|Originals]]'' tour a London newspaper reported that the New Zealanders played as if they were "all ''backs''" which, due to a typographical error, subsequently became "All Blacks".<ref>{{Cite web |title=All Blacks – The Name? |url=http://www.rugbymuseum.co.nz/asp/container_pages/normal_menu/rmArticle.asp?IDID=138 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081014042608/http://www.rugbymuseum.co.nz/asp/container_pages/normal_menu/rmArticle.asp?IDID=138 |archive-date=14 October 2008 |access-date=26 March 2013 |publisher=New Zealand Rugby Museum}}</ref><ref name="Palenski">{{Cite book |last=Palenski |first=Ron |title=Century in Black – 100 Years of All Black Test Rugby |publisher=Hodder Moa Beckett Publishers Limited |year=2003 |isbn=1-86958-937-8 |chapter=p16-17}}</ref> However, the ''Express and Echo'' in Devon, reporting after the Originals match there, referred to "The All Blacks, as they are styled by reason of their sable and unrelieved costume."<ref name="Palenski" />
